notes: The traditional Islamic/Arabic greeting, used any time of day.

en: and upon you be peace (the reply)
notes: The standard reply to as-salāmu ʿalaykum.
Literally "may you wake up well" — said when parting for the night.
Feminine form: حَمْرَاء (ḥamrāʾ) — Arabic color adjectives agree in gender with the noun they describe.
Arabic coffee is a symbol of hospitality — often served with dates when welcoming a guest.

en: a house (subject form, ending in ḍammatayn)
in a house (ending in kasratayn, after a preposition)

example.en: I am a student at the school.
We are going to the restaurant.

notes: Literally "family and ease" — a warm phrase meant to make a guest feel at home.
Family and hospitality sit at the heart of Arab culture — guests are often welcomed like family.
Father's brother. Mother's brother is خَال (khāl).
Father's sister. Mother's sister is خَالَة (khālah).
بَيْضَة is one egg; the collective is بَيْض (bayḍ).
Pairs with the existing جَدِيد (jadīd) "new" — قَدِيم/جَدِيد describes objects; كَبِير/صَغِير (see "old (person)"/"young") describes a person's age.
Arabic has no verb "to have": عِنْدَ ("at / with") takes a possessive suffix — عِنْدِي (I have), عِنْدَهُ (he has).
Points at something masculine. See the grammar point gr:demonstratives.
Plural of هَذَا / هَذِهِ, for people and things.
The noun after it takes the genitive ending. See gr:core-prepositions.
Negates a nominal sentence; the comment after it takes the accusative. See gr:negation-a1.
Same word as the existing "small" (size) adjective — صَغِير covers both a person's age and an object's size, same as كَبِير for "old (person)" / "big".
Same word as the existing "big" (size) adjective — see the note on "young".
Noun form of the existing عَمِلَ (ʿamila) "to work" verb.
Distinct from the existing حَدِيقَة (ḥadīqah) "garden" — مُتَنَزَّه is specifically a public park / recreation area.
Distinct from the existing عَلَى (ʿalā) "on" (lex:prt-02) — فَوْقَ is spatial "above/over"; عَلَى is the general locative "on/at".
Foot; رِجْل (rijl) is leg / foot more broadly.
"Healthy" of food or lifestyle; for a person, بِخَيْر (bikhayr).
الْجَوُّ حَارّ = the weather is hot.
The usual answer to كَيْفَ حَالُك؟ — أَنَا بِخَيْر.

Near-synonym of the existing عَمِلَ (ʿamila) "to work / to do" — فَعَلَ is the more general "do/make" verb, and the paradigm verb Arabic grammar references cite by root ف-ع-ل. Present tense: يَفْعَل (yafʿal).
Feminine: تِلْكَ (tilka). Points at something farther away than هَذَا.
Attaches to the next word: البَيْت وَالْمَدْرَسَة.
The counted noun after كَمْ is singular and accusative: كَمْ كِتَابًا؟
